geometry_edits.rationale: Keep the split-wing reading but make the mass more explicitly separated so the ground threshold can read as a real public interval rather than a compressed seam.
Strengthen the ground relation by emphasizing a continuous base element along the access edge.
Raise the ground condition slightly so the public threshold becomes more legible in section and front view.
Widen the separation enough to create a more readable void/court without breaking the dominant massing idea.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single bent ribbon/split-wing mass in all four views, so it has basic coherence and the protected public-threshold node is doing useful work. However, the form is too compressed and opaque at ground level, with only a small undercut/ledge rather than a convincing public void, court, or entry seam responding to the verified access edge. The dominant gesture is legible but not yet clearly capacity-aware for neighborhood living: the section appears more like an abstract folded object than a grounded mixed-use bar with active frontage and a calm upper hierarchy. It also carries a slight stair-step/cascade impression without enough programmatic consequence, so the silhouette score stays moderate-low. Repair integrity is acceptable because the mass remains continuous and not visibly self-colliding across views, but the program fit fails because the visible section does not yet support the required active street threshold and usable public-space logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Campus/education scale is larger and more dispersed than the candidate; transfer the courtyard-and-bridge principle, not the complexity or spread.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Multi-wing neighborhood massing organized around a legible shared void and connected circulation/terrace logic.
